## 3f600d3093b8

Source SHA-256:
`1e6369fd9067dae9de338776d8498664c307be6545170859093866b35fb6a8f2`.

### Finding A1 — A stored canonical input is rejected

The rule extracts a submatrix selected by 8-marked rows in the first column
and 8-marked columns in the first row. Canonical training example index 3 is:

```
08808
09876
05432
81098
07654
```

Its correct stored output is `[[1,0,8]]`; actual Racket agrees. `self_check`
rejects this exact input with
`expected >=2 row markers (col 0 == 8), found 1`.
A canonical one-selected-row task is therefore outside the generator's
admission and the exact count override also rejects 1. This is not an oracle
label failure: all five canonical pairs agree with Racket.

### Finding A2 — Matrix color 8 and canonical scale are systematically excluded

The interior palette excludes 8 unconditionally, although canonical selected
outputs contain it (training examples 2 and 3). All 128 generated outputs used
colors from {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9}; none contained 8. The source construction makes
this exclusion structural, not just a census miss. Default grids also use
8..12 dimensions instead of the smaller canonical forms. The dominant risk is
incorrectly teaching that marker color cannot be ordinary selected cell data.

### Finding A3 — Advertised controls disagree with runtime behavior

At seed 0, sample 0, medium, independently setting `palette_kind="warm"`,
`palette_size=9`, `n_distinct_colors=9`, `texture="cool"`, or the undeclared
`surprise_unknown_control=True` produces the exact unchanged grid. Declared
boundary `grid_h=6` raises an actual 8..12 range error; declared
`n_row_markers=6` raises an actual 2..4 range error. The public schema is not
an effective generator interface.

Suggested owner action: restore one-marker and interior-8 support, align
published bounds/controls with the actual generator, reject unknown controls,
and retain the canonical input above as a regression. No fixes applied here.
All 128 generated cases passed current self_check and matched an independent
extraction implementation against Racket; this does not invalidate the
admission/distribution findings.

## 3f600d3093b8

**Finding: the ordinary generator excludes a canonical one-row selection case, leaving a perfect minimum-two-markers shortcut.**

The canonical fourth training pair has one row marker and three column markers:

```text
input:  08808 / 09876 / 05432 / 81098 / 07654
output: 108
```

A wrong solver that performs the real submatrix extraction only when there are at least two marked rows and two marked columns, and otherwise returns `[[0]]`, matches all 480 ordinary generated draws I checked across easy/medium/hard (40 seeds × 4 sample indices × 3 bands). Every generated draw had 2–4 row markers and 2–4 column markers. The same shortcut returns `0` on the canonical pair instead of `108`.

This is not merely a dimension mismatch: it permits a model to infer a false structural precondition on the rule and fail a demonstrated canonical branch. The cheapest repair would be to schedule at least one ordinary lesson example with exactly one marked row and at least one with exactly one marked column, while retaining the multi-marker cases. Reproduction and counts are in `checks/audit_probes.json`.
